transcript.content: Hi, I’m glad you came in today. What brings you in today?
I came in because I’ve just been feeling worn out almost every day. Even if I sleep through the night, when I get up for my cashier shift, my body and my head still feel like they’re dragging.
Have you been feeling down or depressed?
I don’t know if I’d call it depressed. I haven’t really noticed feeling down like that, at least not in a clear way.
Have you been having trouble sleeping?

Yeah, most nights. I’ll get into bed tired, but then I’m just lying there thinking about bills, my work schedule, whether everyone at home is okay… that kind of stuff. And even when I do fall asleep, I wake up feeling like I never really settled down.
Do you find yourself worrying a lot on most days?

Yeah, I do. Most days my mind just keeps jumping around—from money, to the relative staying with us, my wife being stressed, church stuff, and then whether I’m messing things up at work. It’s like one worry leads into another.
Have you lost interest in things you usually enjoy?
Not really, no. I still do the things I usually like when I have time. I wouldn’t say I’ve lost interest in them.
When you start worrying, is it hard for you to stop or control the worrying?

Yeah, it is. I’ll tell myself to just pray about it or leave it alone, but once it starts, it kind of keeps going. One worry turns into the next, and before I know it I’m thinking through every bad way the day could go.
Do you often feel physically tense, like your muscles are tight or wound up?
I’m not really sure. I haven’t noticed my muscles being tight like that a lot. I mean, I get uneasy sometimes, but I don’t know if I’d call it being physically tense.
Do you find it hard to concentrate because your mind is preoccupied with worries?
Yeah, sometimes. At the register I can be looking right at the screen, but my mind is on stuff at home or bills, and I lose track. Then I have to recount the drawer or I catch a small mistake I made.
Has this pattern of worrying been going on for at least six months?
Yeah, it’s been more than six months. I’d say about a year and three months now, since our older relative moved in with us.
Have you been feeling more irritable than usual?
I don’t think so, not more than usual. I mean, I can get annoyed like anyone, but I haven’t really noticed being extra irritable.
Have you been feeling hopeless?
I wouldn’t say hopeless, no. I get worried and stressed, but I don’t feel like things are pointless or anything like that.
When you do get a good night’s sleep or some time to rest, do you still feel worn out the next day?

Yeah, I do. Even if I sleep through the night or get time to rest, I still wake up feeling worn out. My body and my head just feel like they’re dragging, and then I have to get up for my cashier shift already tired.
Do you often feel nervous or on edge?

Yeah, pretty often. My mind kind of jumps from one thing to the next—money, the relative staying with us, my wife being stressed, church stuff, and whether I’m messing up at work. It’s hard to feel settled.
Do you get mentally exhausted very easily after doing everyday tasks that require concentration?

Yes, pretty easily. Even normal stuff that takes focus wears me out. That’s kind of why I came in—I feel worn out almost every day, like even after a full night’s sleep my body and my head are still dragging when I have to get up for my cashier shift.
When you’re lying in bed unable to fall asleep, do you feel your body keyed up or unable to relax?

Yeah. Most nights I’m tired when I get into bed, but I can’t really settle. I just lie there thinking about bills, my work schedule, and whether everyone at home is okay. Even when I do fall asleep, it feels like my body never really relaxed.
Do you feel mentally exhausted very quickly, even from ordinary tasks that don’t seem very stressful?

Yes. Even regular things wear me out faster than they should. That’s part of why I came in—I feel worn out almost every day, and even if I sleep through the night, my body and my head still feel dragged down when I get up for my cashier shift.
Does doing mental tasks, like concentrating at work, make your exhaustion noticeably worse?

Yes, it does. When I have to focus at work, like keeping track of the register and customers, I get worn out pretty fast. Even if I slept the night before, by the time I’m getting up for my cashier shift, my body and my head already feel like they’re dragging.
On nights when you’re not caught up in worries, are you still unable to fall asleep?

Usually if I’m not worrying, I can fall asleep better. The problem is most nights I do start going over bills, my work schedule, and whether everyone at home is okay. Then even when I sleep, I wake up feeling like I never really settled down.
After doing small everyday tasks, does it take you a long time to feel recovered again?

Yeah, it does. Even small stuff can leave me feeling worn out longer than I think it should. I’ll do something normal, and afterward my body and my head just feel like they’re dragging, like I’m still not caught up even if I slept okay.
Do you get physically exhausted very easily after even small amounts of physical activity?

Yeah, pretty easily. I mean, I came in because I feel worn out almost every day. Even after a full night’s sleep, my body and my head still feel like they’re dragging when I get up for my cashier shift.
